source_documents.title: Rational Molecular Design for Achieving Persistent and Efficient Pure Organic Room-Temperature Phosphorescence

reference_evidence_units.subject: mFDBP, compound 2
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Source compound list and Fig.3; crystal emission under ambient conditions.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Compound 2 is designated mFDBP, distinct from representative BDBF compound 3. Fig.3 gives mFDBP lifetime 201 ms and phosphorescence yield 17.7%.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Fig.3 visually inspected. The figure-based lifetime is not extracted from SI; graph correspondence to candidate SMILES remains unverified.

reference_evidence_units.quote: These molecules were found to be non-luminescent in the solution and amorphous states but strongly emissive in the crystalline phase in ambient conditions.
reference_evidence_units.subject: Compounds 1-5, including mFDBP
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Solution, amorphous solid and crystalline states at ambient conditions.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The source reports crystallization-induced emission for the named series including compound 2.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: A series-level explicit statement; detailed BDBF controls on p.7 are not target-specific measurements on mFDBP.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the vibrational motions are largely suppressed to block the nonradia- tive decay of T1 as a result of the environmental constraint.
reference_evidence_units.subject: Designed arylphenone series including compound 2
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Crystalline state, compared with non-rigid conditions.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The authors propose that crystalline environmental constraints suppress vibration and nonradiative T1 decay, while reducing oxygen quenching.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: A series-level proposed rigidification mechanism, not direct vibrational dynamics or independent proof that mFDBP matches every BDBF control.

reference_evidence_units.subject: Compounds 1-3 including mFDBP
reference_evidence_units.statement: The source assigns molecules 1-3 more than 70% pi-pi* character in T1 and links that character to slower phosphorescence decay than the n-pi*-dominated comparators 6-8.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: This is a subgroup result, not the full BDBF S1/T2 state diagram or mFDBP-specific SOC constant. Full SI computational results were not inspected.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The calculated energy gaps between S1 and T1 were considerably large for 1–8 (>0.6 eV)
reference_evidence_units.subject: Calculated molecules 1-8 including mFDBP
reference_evidence_units.statement: The authors argue that gaps greater than 0.6 eV block thermally activated reverse ISC and exclude TADF as the explanation for this series' delayed emission.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: This negative finding concerns TADF, not the entire triplet family, which remains supported by phosphorescence.

reference_evidence_units.quote: crystalline powders of mFBDBF (2) showed a more intense green light with a higher FP of 17.7%.
reference_evidence_units.subject: Compound 2, mFDBP
reference_evidence_units.conditions: 365 nm excitation, crystalline powder under ambient conditions; Fig.6.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The reported compound-2 phosphorescence yield is 17.7%; Figure 6B inset independently lists mFDBP at 201 ms and 17.7%.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Fig.6 visually inspected. Prose misspells the abbreviation as mFBDBF; compound number, Fig.3 and Fig.6 identify mFDBP. Do not replace these values with BDBF's 232 ms/34.5%.

reference_evidence_units.quote: No emis- sion decay was detected in the nanosecond range
reference_evidence_units.subject: Synthesized phosphor series including mFDBP
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Nanosecond decay control compared with absence of sample, reported for Fig.S8.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The source reports no detected nanosecond emission decay and interprets the synthesized series as pure phosphors.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: The detection limit is not stated; Fig.S8 was not inspected. Absence of detectable fast fluorescence does not prove its mathematical absence.

reference_evidence_units.quote: these molecules exhibited bright phosphorescence in solutions
reference_evidence_units.subject: pDBP, mFDBP, FBDBT and ClBCZ
reference_evidence_units.conditions: 77 K solution and amorphous samples, low-temperature crystals; main-text description of Figs.S5-S7.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The source reports low-temperature phosphorescence for compound 2 and the named comparison series even outside the crystalline state.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Only the main-text SI description was read; do not transfer BDBF's detailed temperature spectra or oxygen-control ratios to mFDBP.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The large dependence of tP on bp reveals that the molecular-orbital feature of T1 determines the kP.
reference_evidence_units.subject: Arylphenone phosphor series including mFDBP
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Cross-compound comparison of orbital character, lifetimes and calculated phosphorescence rates.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The source's central design argument tunes T1 orbital mixing to balance efficient ISC with a slow radiative phosphorescence rate and long lifetime.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: A cross-series mechanistic interpretation, not a separately measured mFDBP radiative-rate decomposition. Maximum series performance must not be attached to every compound.

reference_mechanisms.label: RIM_RIR_RIV
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Preserve the explicit series-level proposal of vibration suppression in crystals; this is not inferred from AIE terminology alone.

reference_mechanisms.label: PACKING_HOST_MATRIX_CONFINEMENT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Crystallization is the source's enabling rigidification and protection condition for ambient RTP; low-temperature noncrystalline emission bounds the claim.

reference_mechanisms.label: RADIATIVE_RATE_STATE_BALANCE
reference_mechanisms.rationale: The main mechanistic design argument is orbital-character control of the phosphorescence radiative rate while preserving ISC efficiency; mFDBP is explicitly included in the calculated subgroup.

reference_mechanisms.label: TRIPLET_METAL_ENERGY_TRANSFER
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Persistent pure-organic phosphorescence is supported for compound 2 (201 ms, 17.7%). The family is RTP/ISC, not metal emission or TADF.

mechanism_decisions.label: HOST_GUEST_INTERACTION

mechanism_decisions.label: ICT_TICT_CT
mechanism_decisions.rationale: No target-specific ICT/TICT emissive-state assignment is established in the selected evidence.

mechanism_decisions.label: ESIPT_PT

mechanism_decisions.label: PET_ET
mechanism_decisions.rationale: No target-specific photoinduced electron-transfer pathway is established; orbital transitions alone are insufficient.

mechanism_decisions.label: AGGREGATE_EXCITON_EXCIMER
mechanism_decisions.rationale: Aggregation or close contacts do not by themselves establish an aggregate exciton, excimer, exciplex, or H/J excited state.

mechanism_decisions.label: RACI_CI_ACCESS

mechanism_decisions.label: SOKR_ANTI_KASHA
